posts.title: CSS From Scratch
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Fourteen lessons that end with a stylesheet you could hand to somebody else and not have to explain.

This starts at what a token is, so no CSS is assumed. It ends at a build step you probably do not need, which is the most useful lesson in it.

Every lesson is short on purpose. If a thing takes forty minutes to explain, it is two things.

What you will be able to do

  • Read a design system as two tiers of tokens rather than a pile of classes
  • Build a layout with four grid properties instead of a framework
  • Set a type scale you can defend in a review
  • Ration one accent colour so it still means something on page forty
  • Ship motion that is honest under prefers-reduced-motion
  • Write CSS a second person can delete without asking you
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Tokens, layout and type — the whole system, built in front of you.

posts.title: Ghost Themes End to End
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Six lessons on the parts of Ghost theming that the documentation states once and never repeats.

Assumes you have written HTML and CSS. It does not assume you have read a Handlebars helper reference, because nobody has.

The last lesson is the one about gscan and the zip, which is where most first themes die.

What you will be able to do

  • Route a collection with routes.yaml and know why the filter matters
  • Use internal tags as a data model instead of a naming convention
  • Write a post dispatcher that stays readable at twenty layouts
  • Pass gscan the first time
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Handlebars, routes.yaml and a theme you can actually ship.

posts.title: What a design system actually is
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

A design system is the set of decisions you have already made, written down somewhere a second person can find them. The components are the receipt, not the system.

In this lesson

  • Tell a system from a component library in one question
  • Say what a decision costs when it is not written down
  • Find the three decisions every page on a site depends on
If two people can make the same page two ways, you do not have a system yet.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Not a component library. A set of decisions you stop re-making.

posts.title: Two tiers of tokens
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

The first tier holds the values: a grey, a size, a duration. The second gives them jobs. Templates only ever touch the second, which is how you change a colour without opening forty files.

In this lesson

  • Name a token for its job rather than its value
  • Swap a whole theme by rebinding the second tier
  • Spot the token that is secretly two tokens
A token named after what it looks like will be wrong the first time the design changes.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Raw values underneath, meanings on top — and only the top tier gets used.

posts.title: One colour, rationed
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Pick one accent and spend it like money. The moment it lands on both the primary button and the hover state and the active link and the badge, it has stopped pointing at anything.

In this lesson

  • Budget one accent across a full page
  • Choose between colour and weight for emphasis
  • Keep a state colour out of the decoration
Emphasis is a ratio, not a colour.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: An accent that appears everywhere means nothing anywhere.

posts.title: The type scale
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

A scale exists so the answer to how big is this is already decided. If a heading needs a size that is not on it, the layout is asking the wrong question.

In this lesson

  • Build a scale from a ratio rather than a list
  • Make it fluid without losing the steps
  • Say no to the size between two steps
The point of a scale is the sizes it does not contain.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Six sizes, a ratio you can say out loud, and nothing in between.

posts.title: The container and the gutter
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

One maximum width and one gutter, declared once. Everything that lines up on the page lines up because it derives from those two, not because somebody matched a number by eye.

In this lesson

  • Derive every horizontal edge from two custom properties
  • Make a full-bleed section without breaking the column
  • Stop hardcoding a max-width in a template
Two people matching a number by eye is a bug with a long fuse.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Two values that decide every horizontal edge on the site.

posts.title: Grid, in four rules
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

A grid is not a layout system you switch on. It is four properties, and everything else in the specification is a shorthand for one of them.

In this lesson

  • Lay out a responsive grid with one property
  • Say what the implicit grid is doing and why
  • Choose between gap and margin without guessing
  • Match a row of cards without setting a height
Naming areas is a readability decision, not a layout one.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Columns, gap, the implicit grid, alignment. The rest is shorthand.

posts.title: Flex, and when not to reach for it
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Flex is for a row of things whose sizes come from their contents. The moment you are writing widths in percentages, you wanted a grid.

In this lesson

  • Apply the one-dimension test in a second
  • Space a toolbar without a single margin
  • Stop fighting flex-basis
If you are writing percentages into a flex child, you wanted a grid.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: One dimension, content-sized. That is the whole test.

posts.title: Measure and leading
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Leading is a function of measure. Set the line length first and the line height mostly picks itself; do it the other way round and you will be nudging numbers all afternoon.

In this lesson

  • Set a measure in ch and stop guessing
  • Derive leading from length rather than taste
  • Keep a heading tight without cramping a paragraph
A long line with generous leading is still a long line.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Line length first, line height second. In that order, always.

posts.title: Motion that survives a preference
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Every animation needs an answer to what happens when somebody has asked for less of it, and the honest answer is usually nothing at all rather than the same thing, slower.

In this lesson

  • Write a reduced-motion branch that is not just a shorter duration
  • Animate a layout change without moving anything the reader is reading
  • Keep a transition off the main thread
The reduced-motion version is the version that has to still make sense.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Reduced motion is not a smaller animation. It is a different design.

posts.title: The build step you may not need
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Most of what a preprocessor was for is in the platform. What is left is worth a build step; the rest of it is a habit.

In this lesson

  • List what your build actually still does for you
  • Replace three preprocessor features with platform ones
  • Decide whether to keep the step at all
A build step you cannot justify in one sentence is a build step you inherited.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: Custom properties, nesting and layers ship without a compiler now.

posts.title: Routes, collections and the filter
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

A collection is a filter with a permalink. Once that sentence makes sense, routes.yaml stops being a file you copy from somebody else's theme.

In this lesson

  • Route a collection and know why the filter matters
  • Choose between a collection and a taxonomy
  • Keep two collections from claiming the same post
A collection is a filter with a permalink. Everything else is detail.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: routes.yaml in one lesson, filters and all.

posts.title: Internal tags as a data model
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Ghost hands a theme one place to put structure that is not content: internal tags. Used deliberately they are a data model; used carelessly they are a naming convention that rots.

In this lesson

  • Design a tag vocabulary you can still read in a year
  • Carry a value on a tag description when the name cannot hold it
  • Keep internal tags out of the reader's way
A tag scheme nobody wrote down is a naming convention, not a model.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: #hash tags are the only structured field Ghost gives a theme.

posts.title: The post dispatcher
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

post.hbs decides which layout a post gets by asking about its tags, most specific first. Every layout is a partial, so the dispatcher stays a page long no matter how many you add.

In this lesson

  • Write a most-specific-first tag chain
  • Keep a layout partial from knowing about the dispatcher
  • Add the twenty-first layout without touching the twentieth
The dispatcher decides. The layouts do not get a vote.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: One post.hbs, twenty layouts, and no copy-paste.

posts.title: Helpers that carry their weight
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Four helpers do almost everything. Each has one behaviour that will cost you an afternoon the first time, and all four of those are in this lesson.

In this lesson

  • Query with get and know what pagination.total is counting
  • Remember that foreach hides internal tags unless told otherwise
  • Nest a block without silently discarding it
Every one of these helpers fails quietly. That is the thing to know about them.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: get, foreach, has, match — and the traps in each.

posts.title: Members, gates and the honest paywall
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

The gate is Ghost's, not the theme's. What the theme owns is what a locked thing looks like before somebody pays, and being honest there is worth more than the lock.

In this lesson

  • Show a locked lesson without lying about what is behind it
  • Use visibility instead of hiding content in CSS
  • Give a free preview a reason to exist
A paywall that hides how much is behind it converts worse than one that does not.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: What a theme can and cannot do about access.

posts.title: gscan, the zip, and shipping it
posts.mobiledoc:
{"version": "0.3.1", "atoms": [], "cards": [["html", {"html": "

Everything that breaks at upload time breaks for one of five reasons, and gscan names four of them. The fifth is the zip.

In this lesson

  • Read a gscan error to the actual line
  • Build a zip Ghost will accept
  • Keep a theme upgradable across a major version
A theme that passes locally and fails on upload usually packaged the wrong folder.
"}]], "markups": [], "sections": [[10, 0], [1, "p", []]]}
posts.custom_excerpt: The last mile, where most first themes die.
